title: naive AAC splice is rejected

definition.title: naive AAC splice is rejected
definition.source_excerpt: Two separately encoded 3-second stereo AAC-LC ADTS streams were concatenated byte-for-byte. File length is exactly the sum of the inputs, and the concatenated decoder produces the expected total number of samples, but the second segment is not equal to decoding B as its own stream. Maximum float difference is 0.090085; 144,640 sample frames differ above 1e-7. This rejects the naive “compatible headers means raw AAC segments are spliceable” route. Transform overlap and other decoder state must be accounted for, or the player must create an explicit discontinuity/reset instead of pretending the coded streams are continuous.
